MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 13, 2021
Due to COVID-19 and the “Stay at Home” Order for the State of California and the Social
Distance Guidelines issued by Federal, State, and Local Authorities the public was not in
attendance. All public comments that were emailed to the City Clerk were read during the
meeting.

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at
5:00 p.m., on April 13, 2021, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on April 9, 2021, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at
the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Real Property Negotiators: Stein Mart Property 25282 Marguerite
  Parkway; Agency Negotiators: Dennis Wilberg, Keith Rattay, Elaine Lister, Cheryl
  Dyas and William Curley. Negotiating Party: Kinstler Family Trust. Under Negotiation-
  Price and Terms

City Council Minutes  1  April 13, 2021
   Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Shared public information, she herself researched, pertaining to the
  Stein Mart building and Saddleback Lanes.

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel: Existing Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph 4 of
  Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 - Southwest Voter Registration Education Project v.
  The City of Mission Viejo.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:04 p.m. with five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley stated the City is entirely aware of every aspect this speaker noted with
regards to her comments on CS1. He added there is no reportable action, and the City shall continue
to discuss price and terms, as permitted. As to the CS2 item, the City shall continue to look at its
legal progress and options, but there was no reportable action.

INVOCATION: Council Member Goodell

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Sachs

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

 AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
 NOES:  None
 ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  (1) Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of March 23, 2021, as
  presented (2) approved the Minutes for the Special City Council Meeting of March 31, 2021,
  as presented, and (3) approved the Minutes for the Adjourned Meeting/Joint Housing Element
  Kick-off Workshop with the City Council and Planning and Transportation Commission of
  March 31, 2021, as presented or as amended.

2.  Check Register Dated March 12, 2021 in the Amount of $855,645.59

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  2  April 13, 2021
 3.  Check Register dated March 19, 2021 in the amount of $831,592.41

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated March 26, 2021 in the Amount of $991,725.70

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register Dated April 2, 2021 in the Amount of $420,205.87

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February 2021

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for February 2021

  Received and filed.

8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for February 2021

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February
  2021

  Received and filed.

10. Contract Amendment for Painting and Related Services at City Facilities.

  Approved first amendment for Signature Painting for painting and related services at city
  facilities in an amount not to exceed $15,000.00.

11. Citywide Systemic Safety Analysis Report Program (SSARP) & Local Road Safety Plan
  (LRSP) Project

  (1) Authorized the City Manager to execute a Professional Services Consultant Team (PSCT)
  contract with Kittelson & Associates, Inc.; and (2) Authorized the issuance of a purchase order
  to Kittelson & Associates, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $249,964 for engineering services
  for the subject project.

12. La Paz Bridge/Road Widening (CIP 756) - MNWD Reclaimed Water Pipeline
  Agreement

City Council Minutes  3  April 13, 2021
   Authorized the City Manager to approve an agreement with the Moulton Niguel Water District
  to incorporate the construction of a reclaimed water pipeline connection into the subject
  project.

13. Purchase and Installation of a Pelican Wireless HVAC Control System for the Council
  Chamber and Lobby Air Conditioning Equipment at the City of Mission Viejo City Hall

  Awarded contract to Tri-Pacific Heating & Air Conditioning LP for the period of April 20,
  2021 to September 30, 2021 in the amount of $21,728.00 for the purchase and installation of
  a Pelican Wireless HVAC Control System for the Council Chamber and Lobby Air
  Conditioning Equipment at the City of Mission Viejo City Hall.

14. Purchase, Installation and Upgrades to the Fire Alarm System at the City of Mission
  Viejo City Hall

  Awarded contract to Pyro-Comm Systems, Inc. for the period of April 20, 2021 to September
  30, 2021 in the amount of $55,430.00 for the purchase, installation and upgrades to the fire
  alarm system at the City of Mission Viejo City Hall.

15. Cleaning Services Relative to COVID-19 Pandemic for all City Playgrounds and Park
  Restrooms

  (1) Approved the Second Amendment to the existing Landscape Maintenance Contract Area
  #6 with Nieves Landscape, Inc for the subject services; (2) approved the Third Amendment
  to the existing Landscape Maintenance Contract Area #9 with Landscape West Management
  Services, Inc for the subject services; (3) authorized issuance of a contract change order to
  Nieves Landscape, Inc. in the amount not to exceed $110,000.00; (4) authorized issuance of
  a contract change order to Landscape West Management Services, Inc. in the amount not to
  exceed $20,000.00; and (5) adopted resolution 21-09 Amending the FY 2020/21 City Budget.

16. Software Licensing Renewal for the Animal Services Center

  Approved issuance of a purchase order to HLP, Inc. in the amount of $33,837.60 for purchase
  of software licensing and maintenance support for the Animal Services Center.

17. Firewall Security Subscription Renewal

  Approved purchase order for Cisco Firewall security subscription 1-year renewal to Resilient
  Communications Inc. in the amount of $32,158.80.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

City Council Minutes  4  April 13, 2021
 OLD BUSINESS

18. General Plan Progress Report for 2020

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented the staff report.

  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum asked for an update on the next General Plan. Director Lister
  referenced the Joint Housing Element Kick-Off Workshop between the City Council and
  Planning and Transportation Commission which took place on March 31.

  She stated some rezoning will most likely take place, and the Regional Housing Needs
  Assessment (RHNA) update shall be presented before the Council in the coming months as it
  is due to the State in October.

  By Consensus the report was received and filed.

 19. FY 2021-2023 Revenue Projections

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum mentioned that it has been brought to her attention that apparently
  gas prices are higher by 25 cents in Mission Viejo than surrounding cities and questioned if
  that was true. She also asked about the projection for the reminder of the year with regards
  to the recreation membership fees. Director Dyas stated that projections are constantly
  changing, and the revenue projection will change, as will expenditures with facilities opening
  sooner than expected. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum asked City Manager Dennis Wilberg
  about staffing at these facilities. Mr. Wilberg clarified there is misrepresentation in the
  community, that the Norman. P. Murray Community and Senior Center is closed due to
  budget problems, which is not the case. He went on to mention, that staff has been working
  very hard behind the scenes, and is on track to reopen at the beginning of May, although not
  completely at pre-Covid levels. This will include bringing back some fitness classes, opening
  the lounge, and enabling outside organizations to hold monthly meetings. Per the Governor’s
  timeline, staff is working on a plan to expand services with a phased-in approach.

  Mayor Kelley asked Director Dyas for any information she could share on the ARP (American
  Rescue Plan). Director Dyas stated that the projected amount is still $9.52 Million, which
  will be received in two installments, the first being next month and the second approx. May
  2022.

  By Consensus the report was received and filed.

20. Sixty (60) Day Extension of Exclusive Right to Negotiate Agreement-Stein Mart

  Robert D. Breton, M.V.: Outlined some of the challenges in dealing with twelve different
  owners at the Village Center. He supports the recommended action and encourages the City
  Council to proceed with the property negotiations.

  City Attorney Bill Curley stated that the City has been pursuing the Core Area Vision Plan
  for several years. In order to implement this vision, the City is looking to acquire the Stein
City Council Minutes  5  April 13, 2021
   Mart property. He has been working diligently to come to an agreement on price and terms,
  and is asking the Council to consider and grant the extension, so that staff can put together a
  presentation for public consideration, the purchase and sale agreement.

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister & Assistant City Manager/Director of
  Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum asked for clarification if the Vison Plan includes any housing.
  Assistant City Manager Rattay stated that it does not.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve
  60-day extension of Exclusive Right to Negotiate Agreement-Stein Mart.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

21. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Sachs had nothing to report.

22. Transportation Corridor Agency (TCA) Report

  Received report from Mayor Kelley.

23. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Goodell.

CITY MANAGER REPORT

City Manager Dennis Wilberg complemented the OCTA on how hard they have worked with
regards to adjusting the maintenance of effort requirement, and stay true to information that the
voters approved when they renewed Measure M. He also emphasized that the City is continuing to
reopen facilities. The Library, including passport services, opened via appointment only, and in
early May the City plans to open both the Library and the Norman P. Murray Community and
Senior Center. Staff are also working on expanding the hours of operation at Montanoso and Sierra
Recreation and Fitness Centers, and the two tennis complexes.

CITY ATTORNEY REPORT

City Attorney Bill Curley stated that the majority of his time has been focused on the Housing
Element General Plan obligations and the Stein Mart property.

City Council Minutes  6  April 13, 2021
 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

24. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell stated that the Swim Meet held at the Marguerite Aquatics complex this
past weekend was fantastic, and went off without a hitch. He was excited to volunteer and be able
see some top athletes that will probably participate it the Tokyo Olympics.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths said it’s good to be back in the Chambers. He went on to congratulate the
one property owner that owns the area by Delizie, Harmony Tea, Kwik Kopy and Callie Girl, who
has done a great job in making a little village, inside a big village. Council Member Raths added
that he has met with a few potential business owners in the hopes of bringing new business back to
Mission Viejo and is excited about revitalizing the Village Area. He also thanked OC Supervisors
Do and Wanger for not requiring any type of vaccination passport in government buildings in the
County. Council Member Raths congratulated Tam Nguyen on his appointment to the Orange
County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Board of Directors. Lastly, he commented on the expose
of former Mission Viejo resident and pro golfer Mark O’Meara right before the Masters this past
Sunday.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs commented on the two software licensing proposals that were passed on
the Consent Calendar today, and he would like to see if we can come up with an independent audit
of Information Technology (IT) licensing. He questioned if there is other software we should be
using instead of renewing licenses. He would like another perspective, and is not being accusatory,
but stated, of all the departments, IT is the fastest growing area and wants to make sure we are
keeping up with the latest technology. He asked that this be agendaized at a future meeting for
discussion. Council Member Sachs concluded by agreeing with his fellow Council Members that
the Swim meet was a great event, and wanted to recognize City Manager, Dennis Wilberg, for his
conversations with County Manager Frank Kim, at the eleventh hour making sure the event went
off without a hitch, great job.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum shared that she attended the Swim Meet all three days, and noted that a
lot of organization went into putting this event on. She also read a statement from Supervisor Lisa
Bartlett, stating that Orange County will not be adopting any kind of proof of vaccination
requirements. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum reminded everyone of upcoming events; Saturday,
April 17, drive-through Food Drive at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center from
9:00 -11:00am, April 19-25, the Virtual Comic Fest takes every place night via Zoom from 6:30 -

City Council Minutes  7  April 13, 2021
 7:30pm and on Saturday, April 24, drive-through National Prescription Drug Take-Back Day at
City Hall from 10:00am -2:00pm and the Compost Giveaway at the Mission Viejo Animal Services
Center parking lot, 28095 Hillcrest, from 11:00 am – Noon.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley echoed the praise for Mr. Wilberg and Mr. Rattay on their efforts to pull off this
extraordinary Swim Meet, and on a national stage, plus recognized coach Mr. Mark Schubert for
his hard work. She commended Director of Library and Cultural Services Genesis Hanson, for her
amazing job of preparing the Library for its reopening, and Director of Recreation and Community
Services Mark Nix, in recognizing the demand to reserve swimming lanes and adding additional
hours. Mayor Kelley added, that City staff has done a really good job in keeping the services and
facilities open during the pandemic. She gave an update on virtual Job Fair, which was a wonderful
success with 846 job seekers, 156 employers, and 3,790 job openings, and thanked Todd Kaylish,
a Mission Viejo resident, and the Saddleback Church for partnering with the County on this event.
Mayor Kelley reminded residents that almost everyone can get their vaccination now, and has
requested the City develop a flier with all the pertinent information of how to register for the
vaccination. She asked, that anyone who wished to volunteer in distributing these fliers, to reach
out to her personally. Mayor Kelley concluded by saying it’s really good to be back in the Council
Chamber after a year, and welcomed the public back, safely, at the next City Council meeting. It
has been quite a difficult year, but also a year that has brought out the best in people.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:59 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Tuesday April 27, at 5:00 p.m.

Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of April 27, 2021

City Council Minutes  8  April 13, 2021
